title: Little Hagia Sophia
visualBrief: Individual medium-fi Little Hagia Sophia exterior: mixed brick/stone low body and projecting eastern apse, raised buttressed brick drum, shallow grey lead central dome, western five-bay round-arched open portico with five small roof domes, pale single-balcony minaret and green side door. Exact main outline retained; all internal partitions, heights, roof plans and tower position are estimates. Six existing shared 256² graphs, seven merged roles and four budgeted browser LODs. Separate tomb, cemetery, school, city, fine ornament and furnished interiors remain outside this asset.

sourceFacts.horizontalBasis: Retained exact way 303179753 / Q1144576 is current viewer building 35184675268585. Its 16 current outer vertices, original anchor and heading remain fixed. Positive X points approximately east-southeast toward the apse; negative X toward the west-northwest entrance/portico. Positive Z is approximately south-southwest. A western five-bay portico is divided at estimated local X=-17; this is an architectural partition within the raw main footprint, not independent map data. The raised central drum/dome is centered near [3.5,0.1], with the single minaret near the northwest narthex corner [-13,-9.8]. Main roof divisions, portico bay positions, minaret plan and detailed side/rear openings are picture estimates. Current/retained heights and independent roof/tower controls are absent. Separate round building 35184902709509 north of the mosque, cemetery, court, schools and city remain host content.
sourceFacts.architecturalHeights: No retained or current map height values exist. Visualization estimates: main eaves 11.8 m; raised sixteen-sided brick drum/buttresses from 12–19.2 m; shallow lead-covered central dome 19.2–23.4 m and finial 24.8 m. Portico capitals 4.9 m, round arches to 6.8 m, roof/cornice 7.8 m and five small shallow domes to about 9.4 m. Single minaret: square base 7 m, tapering pale shaft to 23 m, projecting balcony around 23–24.2 m, smaller upper shaft to 28 m, conical lead cap to 31.4 m and finial 32 m. All these vertical dimensions, roof profiles, small finials, window rhythms and the exact tower origin are explicit picture-led approximations, not surveyed facts. Fine stone capitals, historic brick lattice, calligraphy and unseen interiors omitted.
